mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 20-day SPX returns is negative or below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE rising >0.1pp and HOUST falling >50 units) occurs but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of FEDFUNDS rising >0.2pp over 3 months, INDPRO decline and SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Higher nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) reflects a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS against 5-day SPX returns is negative or below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units indicate a weakening housing market, reducing consumer wealth and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1300.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals dual economic and monetary stress, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE change > 0.1pp and FEDFUNDS change > 0.1pp in the past month
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE rising >0.1pp and FEDFUNDS rising >0.1pp) occurs but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth >3%), a decline in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) signals consumer sector weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of GDPC1 growth >3%, RSAFS decline and SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
